subject.title: Feishu auto-reply and `message` tool path bypass `message_sending` / `reply_payload_sending` / `message_sent` plugin hooks

question: Should this Feishu report be split across the existing outbound hook parity trackers, or should maintainers define a Feishu-specific hook bridge plus a new normal-inbound `inbound_claim` contract here?
rationale: The confirmed gaps span an existing channel-reply hook bypass, the broader outbound sent-hook umbrella, and a binding-only inbound claim design that may intentionally protect ownership semantics.

options.title: Coordinate through existing parity trackers
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/92374 and its candidate PR for `message_sending`, use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/50126 for sent-hook parity, and keep this issue as Feishu-specific proof plus the inbound-claim decision point.

options.title: Create a Feishu-specific bridge
options.body: Repair Feishu's direct dispatcher locally, but require explicit tests and review for double-firing and post-send observation before landing.

options.title: Define normal inbound claims broadly
options.body: Promote `inbound_claim` beyond plugin-owned bindings for all channel inbound, accepting a plugin API behavior change that needs docs and compatibility review.

recommendation.title: Coordinate through existing parity trackers
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/92374 and its candidate PR for `message_sending`, use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/50126 for sent-hook parity, and keep this issue as Feishu-specific proof plus the inbound-claim decision point.

likelyOwner.reason: Current central source history and the most recent broad refactor of the relevant dispatch/outbound files point to this owner as the best first routing candidate.
